sentences.text: Kryptops was an extinct genus of abelisaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of Niger, estimated to have been between 6 and 7 meters in length.

This large carnivorous dinosaur possessed robust upper jaws and highly serrated teeth, while the outer surface of the maxilla features grooves and rugosities suggesting it was covered in a keratinous structure rather than scales.

The preserved maxilla has a tooth row length of 15 centimeters but is missing its tip and some tooth sockets, though the left maxilla preserves 11 tooth positions but likely held 17 or 18 when complete.

The rough texture of the skull implies a keratinous covering on the maxillae rather than scales, a unique anatomical feature referenced by the generic name Kryptops, which means "covered face" in Ancient Greek.

Only a single specimen of Kryptops is currently known to science, consisting of a maxilla collected 15 meters away from a set of postcranial elements including vertebrae, ribs, the sacrum, and the pelvis.
Fossils were collected in 2000 by a University of Chicago expedition led by Paul Sereno, and the genus and species were described in 2008 by Paul Sereno and Steve Brusatte.

The fossils were designated as the holotype specimen for the new genus and species Kryptops palaios, which includes a maxilla with teeth, vertebrae, ribs, and the pelvic girdle and sacrum belonging to an adult approximately 6 to 7 meters long.
Kryptops was a large carnivorous dinosaur with robust upper jaws and highly serrated teeth, indicating a diet of meat.

Kryptops belongs to the family Abelisauridae, a group of theropod dinosaurs that lived from the Jurassic through the Cretaceous until the mass extinction event, and is considered one of the oldest-known abelisaurids.

Researchers noted that the maxilla of Kryptops displays a mix of traits found in both early and late Cretaceous abelisaurids, and Sereno and Brusatte conducted a cladistic analysis to demonstrate that Kryptops was the most basal member of the family Abelisauridae based on characteristics including a textured maxilla with vascular groove impressions and a narrow preorbital fossa.

The fossils date to the Aptian and Albian ages of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago, though the fossil record for Kryptops spans from 121.4 to 100.5 million years ago, and Kryptops lived in what is now Africa during the late Cretaceous, approximately 115 to 110 million years ago.

Kryptops likely inhabited habitats dominated by inland floodplains or riparian zones, sharing its environment with theropods including the carcharodontosaurid Eocarcharia, the spinosaurid Suchomimus, and the noasaurid Afromimus, as well as megaherbivores such as the hadrosauriforms Ouranosaurus and Lurdusaurus, the dryosaurid Elrhazosaurus, and the sauropods Nigersaurus and an unnamed titanosaur.
The aquatic fauna found in Kryptops' habitat consisted entirely of freshwater inhabitants.

In 2012, researchers suggested Kryptops palaios might be a chimera where postcranial remains belong to a carcharodontosaurid like Eocarcharia, and Carrano and colleagues argued that Kryptops palaios is a chimera, suggesting its postcranial remains found 15 meters from the holotype maxilla actually belong to a carcharodontosaurid, possibly Eocarcharia dinops.
In 2018, Rafael Delcourt questioned the validity of Kryptops, suggesting it may be a nomen dubium due to having only one unique feature.
Researchers suggested that metriacanthosaurids radiated globally during the Early Cretaceous based on the simultaneous presence of related fossils in Europe, Africa, and Asia.
